# Dataset

This section will introduce you to our dataset and how to prepare it for `MaAsLin3` from a `phyloseq` object.

## Durance river data
![](images/france_ibm.png){style="width: 200px; border-radius:5px;  background-color: white; border: 5px solid white" fig-align="center"}

We will use the same dataset from the Durance river as the [R community analysis workshop](https://neof-workshops.github.io/R_community_whqkt8/Course/02-Dataset_and_workflow.html#dataset).

We will use MaAsLin3 to determine the differential abundance and prevalence of genera between the sites and the media.
These groupings are:

- `site`: UD (Upper Durance), MD (Middle Durance), and LD (Lower Durance)
- `media`: ENV (Environmental samples, no media), CVP, KBC, and TSA

## Jupyter notebook
![](images/jupyter_notebook.png){style="width:150px; background:white; border-radius:5px; border: white solid 5px" fig-align="center"}

Create and open a new `jupyter` notebook called "1-Data.ipynb"

::: {.callout-important}
Ensure all notebooks for this part are created in your `~/adv_R_comm/maaslin3` directory.
:::

At the top create a markdown cell with the following headers.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# 1-Data
## Libraries
```

Then load all the libraries we need in a new code cell along with the `phyloseq` object containing our dataset.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#Libraries
library("phyloseq")
library("tidyverse")
library("microbiome")
#Data
load("/pub14/tea/nsc206/NEOF/R_community/data/phyloseq.RData")
```

Please create other useful markdown cells in this and future notebooks.
